listen.explanationKey: Who was the United States’ main rival during the Cold War?
facts: After World War II, the United States and the Soviet Union became rivals. This was called the Cold War.
It is called “cold” because the two countries never fought each other directly in a big war. They competed with weapons, money and ideas.
The Soviet Union was communist. Under communism, the government owns the farms, factories and stores, and decides what people make and buy. People have little freedom to choose.
The United States was worried about communism spreading to other countries.
Both countries had nuclear weapons, so people also feared a nuclear war.

listen.explanationKey: Why did the United States enter the Korean War?
facts: Under communism, the government owns and controls almost everything, and people have little freedom. During the Cold War, the United States tried to stop communism from spreading to more countries.
In 1950, communist North Korea invaded South Korea. The United States entered the Korean War to help South Korea.
In Vietnam, communist North Vietnam fought to take over South Vietnam. The United States sent soldiers to help South Vietnam.
Tip: the answer to both questions is the same: to stop the spread of communism. If you forget, remember the Cold War story.
